title: The Cash Payments Journal
summary: The purpose and layout of the Cash Payments Journal (CPJ), recording payments by EFT and cheque in the correct columns, the Sundry accounts column and totalling the journal.

notes.text: The **Cash Payments Journal (CPJ)** is the book of first entry in which all **payments made from the bank account** are recorded. The source documents are **EFT payment notices**, **cheque counterfoils** and the **bank statement** (for debit orders and bank charges).

notes.caption: Cash Payments Journal of Thandi's Hair Salon, March 2025 (CPJ 3)

items: **Name of payee**: the person or business that was paid.
**Analysis columns** (e.g. Wages, Stationery): for expenses that happen often.
**Sundry accounts**: for less frequent payments, such as buying equipment, paying a telephone account, drawings or repaying a loan.

notes.title: Checking the totals
notes.problem: Check that the CPJ above balances.

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: **Drawings** (the owner taking money for personal use) is NOT an expense of the business. It is recorded in the Sundry accounts column with 'Drawings' as the details.

Some payments are made directly by the bank, such as **bank charges** and **debit orders** (e.g. insurance). They are found on the **bank statement** and recorded in the CPJ using 'B/S' (bank statement) in the Doc column.

notes.title: Bank balance at the end of the month
notes.problem: Thandi's bank balance on 1 March was R0. The CRJ total for March is R58 500 and the CPJ total is R15 000. What is the bank balance on 31 March?

notes.text: A **favourable** balance means there is money in the account (an asset). An **unfavourable** balance (bank overdraft) means more has been paid out than was available; it is a **liability**.
